scope: Theorem 3.2 (Pippenger–Spencer) of the manuscript “Nearly minimal maxima and positive minima of Littlewood polynomials” (preprints/Nearly-minimal-maxima-and-positive-minima-of-Littlewood-polynomials-October-5-2026/littlewood-lower-envelope.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 076 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 639fe69dbb6e6e93), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each integer r ≥ 2 and each γ > 0, there is β > 0 such that the following holds. If an r-uniform hypergraph satisfies, for some D > 0, (1 − β)D < d(v) < (1 + β)D for every vertex v, d(u, v) < βD for u ̸= v, then its edges can be partitioned into at most (1 + γ)D matchings.
